title: The Silent Logs

beats.narrativeText: A small communications terminal flickers back to life for the first time in years. It has been waiting, quietly, with fragments of the expedition's logs still inside it.

Whole sections of the recovered logs are corrupted — not randomly damaged, but missing in a way that feels almost deliberate. Something happened here before communications stopped, and the logs are only telling part of it.
The learner reads through the recovered logs carefully, gathering every clue the damaged fragments still hold.
Piece by piece, the learner arranges the events into order and highlights whatever evidence matters most — and a shape starts to form out of the fragments.
The learner must separate what the damaged logs actually confirm from what merely seems likely — Explorer Academy has no interest in a good guess dressed up as a fact.
Piecing the last fragments together, a name finally surfaces from the static: Dr. Elara Quinn. Until now, the expedition has been a mystery without a face — this is the first time it has had one.
The learner reflects on what the logs reveal, and on how many questions a single name can raise all at once.
The expedition mystery has officially begun. Dr. Quinn's name is only the first piece — and the learner already senses it's a much bigger puzzle than one communications terminal can explain.

activities.title: Read Recovered Logs
activities.storyContext: The terminal has been dark for years. Now it's flickering with static and fragments of the expedition's own logs.
activities.instructions: Read through the recovered log fragments carefully, even the parts that seem like static or nonsense at first — some of the most important details are easy to miss on a quick read.
activities.output: Notes on what each log fragment reveals.

activities.title: Arrange Events Chronologically
activities.storyContext: The logs came back damaged and out of order — right now, the sequence of events is anyone's guess.
activities.instructions: Using the clues in each log fragment, arrange the events into the order you think they actually happened.

activities.title: Highlight Important Evidence
activities.storyContext: Not every detail in the logs matters equally — part of the job is knowing which ones do.
activities.instructions: Go back through your notes and highlight the pieces of evidence that seem most important to understanding what actually happened.
activities.output: A list of highlighted key evidence.

activities.title: Separate Facts From Assumptions
activities.storyContext: Explorer Academy values evidence over assumption — even an assumption that feels almost certain is still just an assumption.
activities.instructions: Sort your findings into two honest lists: confirmed facts the logs actually state, and reasonable assumptions you're filling in yourself.
activities.output: Two lists: confirmed facts and assumptions.

activities.title: Rewrite a Damaged Log Entry
activities.storyContext: Each expedition member would have experienced these events differently.
activities.instructions: Choose one damaged log entry and rewrite it from another expedition member's point of view.

activities.title: Reconstructing Incomplete Records
activities.storyContext: Reconstructing the expedition's logs is similar to how historians work with incomplete records.
activities.instructions: Find out how historians reconstruct incomplete historical records.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What's one fact you're certain of from the logs — and one thing you're only assuming, even if it feels likely?

discussionPoints: What clues helped you work out the correct order of events?
How can you tell the difference between a fact and an assumption?
parentGuide.assessment: Look for a logically ordered sequence of events and a clear, justified separation between confirmed facts and assumptions.

completionCriteria: Recovered logs read, events arranged chronologically, and key evidence separated from assumptions.
